bib.title: NeedleBench: Evaluating LLM Retrieval and Reasoning Across Varying Information Densities

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; error-example prompt figures (App H, Figs 13-17) skimmed only

question: How well do LLMs retrieve and reason over long contexts when the relevant information is sparse versus dense?
hypothesis: Passing needle-in-a-haystack retrieval does not imply robust reasoning in information-dense long contexts.
contributions: Comprehensive bilingual long-context benchmark (info-sparse and info-dense)
Ancestral Trace Challenge, an information-dense task

method.summary: Synthetic bilingual benchmark: sparse tasks (single/multi-needle retrieval, multi-needle reasoning) insert fictional needles into essay filler at varied depths and lengths; the dense ATC task is a shuffled set of 2-512 kinship statements with no filler. Instruction-tuned open and closed models evaluated at 32K and 128K.

datasets.name: NeedleBench
datasets.source: Synthetic needles; PaulGrahamEssays (EN) and ChineseDomainModelingEval (ZH) as filler
datasets.preprocessing: Token lengths by GPT-4 tokenizer (tiktoken); buffer subtracted from target length to avoid instruction truncation

models.name: Qwen-1.5/2.5 families, Gemma-3 4/12/27B, LLaMA-3.1 8B/70B, GLM, InternLM, Mistral, Mixtral, Zephyr, DeepSeek-R1 and distills, QwQ-32B, OREAL-32B, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o3-mini, o4-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet-Thinking

inference.prompting: zero-shot task instruction; reasoning and ATC prompts include 3 worked examples and require final answer in \boxed{}

parameters.needle depths and lengths: 32K set: 1k to 32k; 128K set: 1k to 128k, depth percent 0-100 (read from Figs 2,3)

other.engines: LMDeploy and vLLM; closed models via API

metrics.name: keyword-aware Exact Match
metrics.definition: 100 if any core keyword appears in prediction, else 0; averaged over lengths, depths, repeats; Multi-Reasoning uses content of \boxed{}

metrics.name: ATC weighted average
metrics.definition: EM accuracy weighted by needle count

metrics.name: ENL-50
metrics.definition: largest needle count N with EM >= 50%

eval.protocol: 10 repeats, no significance test; ~10% of ATC errors manually annotated

prompts.text: This is a test of long-text capability. You need to first read the long document below, and then answer the final question based on the information in the document.

Here is a test for multi-step reasoning ability called the Ancestral Trace Challenge. In this test, we will simulate different people’s familial relationships, and your task is to continuously reason through them until you identify the eldest ancestor.

limits: Synthetic benchmark; may not reflect real-world complexity (authors)
ATC contexts are short (max ~9.6K tokens), so it tests dense reasoning more than length
Under-thinking taxonomy from manual annotation of ~10% of errors on eldest-ancestor questions only
Closed model sizes and exact versions unspecified; no max_tokens, no significance tests
Memorization explanation for v1 vs v2 gap is not isolated from task-difficulty differences

terms.definition: the inability to sustain inference by fully leveraging all relevant information, resulting in reasoning that halts midway under the mistaken belief that nothing more can be inferred
largest number of needles N for which exact-match accuracy remains at least 50%
